posts.text:
I made a mistake.

When Jack and I decided to organize this $100K Hackathon, my biggest concern was cheating.

Unlike a regular hackathon, everyone participates from home. And because the winner is whoever makes the most PROFIT (not revenue), there are so many ways to manipulate the numbers.

So I added a $99 entry fee.

One thing I’ve learned from building businesses is that people tend to be more committed when they pay for something.

I thought it would filter out spam, attract serious builders, and make the competition fairer for everyone.

But I completely missed the other side.

3 years ago, I was a living with my apps. Today, I’m financially free. My life changed so much that somewhere along the way, I lost perspective on what $99 means to someone else.

For someone in India, someone struggling to pay their bills, or someone trying to make their first dollar online, $99 can be a lot of money.

And those are exactly the people I want to help!

I’ve spent years sharing what I’ve learned, reviewing random people’s landing pages, and organizing free meetups around the world. Not because there’s money to make, but because I genuinely love seeing people build things and succeed.

And somehow, I was so focused on keeping cheaters out that I didn’t realize I was also keeping genuine builders out.

That’s my mistake.

So I’ve decided to make the $100K Hackathon completely FREE :)

Everyone who already paid got a full refund.

I’m still worried about cheating. That problem hasn’t disappeared, and Jack and I will have to figure out better ways to verify profits and keep the leaderboard fair.

But that’s our problem to solve.

Thank you to everyone who shared their thoughts. Sometimes you need people to remind you of things you’ve forgotten.

I genuinely hope this hackathon changes someone’s life.

❤️
posts.text_zh:
我犯了一个错。

当 Jack 和我决定举办这次 $100K Hackathon 时，我最大的担忧是作弊。

和普通黑客松不同，每个人都在家里参赛。而且因为赢家是谁赚到的 PROFIT（利润）最多（不是营收），所以有太多办法可以操纵数字。

所以我加了 99 美元的报名费。

我从做生意中学到的一件事是：人们为某件事付了钱，往往会更认真投入。

我以为这能过滤掉垃圾报名、吸引认真的 builder，并让比赛对所有人都更公平。

但我完全忽略了另一面。

3 年前，我还在靠自己的应用过活。如今我已经财务自由。我的生活变化太大，一路走来，我渐渐失去了对「99 美元对别人意味着什么」的体感。

对一个在印度的人、一个正在为账单发愁的人，或一个想在网上赚到第一美元的人来说，99 美元可能是很大一笔钱。

而他们恰恰是我想帮助的人！

这些年来我一直在分享自己学到的东西、帮陌生人看落地页，还在世界各地组织免费线下聚会。不是因为能赚到钱，而是因为我真心喜欢看到人们把东西做出来并获得成功。

不知怎的，我太专注于把作弊者挡在门外，以至于没意识到自己也把真正的 builder 挡在了门外。

这就是我的错。

所以我决定让这场 $100K Hackathon 完全免费 :)

所有已经付过钱的人都收到了全额退款。

我仍然担心作弊。这个问题并没有消失，Jack 和我必须想出更好的办法来核实利润、保证排行榜公平。

但那是我们该解决的问题。

感谢所有分享想法的人。有时候你需要别人提醒你那些已经忘掉的事。

我真心希望这场黑客松能改变某个人的人生。

❤️

引用内容：他引用了自己早前宣布 The $100K Hackathon 的帖子：Higgsfield 出资 10 万美元，参赛者从 11 月 16 日起用 30 天做一个能盈利的数字产品，奖金包括 10 万美元现金、iPhone Duo 和 MacBook Neo；原先报名费是 99 美元（开赛后 149 美元），与 @jackfriks 共同举办。
